findings.prompt_en: Walk forward on a number line: 1, 2, 3... Which do you reach later, 3 or 7? So which is more?
findings.key: 7 comes later, so 7 is more (acceptable: '7 is more','7','seven','saat','सात')
findings.mine: 7 later, 7 more (EN); for the Hindi wording the first part is 3
findings.why: Languages ask opposite things. prompt_en: 'Which do you reach LATER, 3 or 7?' (7). prompt_hi: 'Pehle 3 aayega ya 7?' = 'Which comes FIRST, 3 or 7?' (3). A child answering the Hindi correctly says '3 ... 7 zyada'; the key text '7 comes later' only fits the English. Final part (which is more = 7) is the same in both. Fix: 'Baad mein kaun aayega, 3 ya 7?'

hinglish.phrase: Kinke kinaare sirf mude hue hain?
hinglish.why: 'mude hue' means bent/folded, not curved; for 'only curved edges' a teacher would say 'gol kinaare' / 'ghumaavdaar kinaare'. Mild, but a book with a folded corner fits the literal Hindi.
